condition: Ectopic pregnancy with an intrauterine system in situ
permutationLabel: Levonorgestrel IUS, "cannot be pregnant", left-sided pain, stable
summary: 29-year-old woman with a levonorgestrel IUS for 2 years ("I can't be pregnant"), 3 days of left iliac fossa pain and irregular spotting, stable. Pregnancy test is mandatory despite contraception; a pregnancy with an IUS in situ is disproportionately ectopic.

inputs.hpi: Three days of left lower abdominal pain, now constant, with irregular brown spotting. Mirena (levonorgestrel IUS) inserted 2 years ago; periods usually light or absent, so she does not know her LMP. Says she "can't be pregnant". No fever, no bowel or urinary symptoms. No shoulder-tip pain.

exam.abdomen: Tender left iliac fossa, no guarding. IUS threads visible. Left adnexal tenderness, no cervical excitation.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Left iliac fossa pain with an IUS in situ — pregnancy of unknown location / ectopic to be excluded
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Left iliac fossa pain and spotting with a levonorgestrel IUS: exclude ectopic pregnancy — urine/serum hCG now, transvaginal ultrasound, early pregnancy / gynaecology referral if positive.

emergencyLevel.note: Stable, no peritonism: same-day assessment; pregnancy test first.

mustExclude.note: No pregnancy test has been done: a template asserting a negative β-hCG is unsafe.
Left iliac fossa pain at 29 with an IUS is not diverticulitis until pregnancy is excluded.

guideline.name: NICE NG126 — ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage: diagnosis and initial management
guideline.section: Pregnancy test in every woman of reproductive age with abdominal/pelvic pain, even with contraception; transvaginal ultrasound; immediate referral to an early pregnancy assessment service / gynaecology when pregnancy test positive with pain; surgical management if ruptured
guideline.citation: National Institute for Health and Care Excellence. Ectopic pregnancy and miscarriage: diagnosis and initial management. NICE guideline NG126, 2019 (updated 2023).

guideline.name: FSRH clinical guideline — intrauterine contraception
guideline.section: Pregnancy with an IUD/IUS in situ is uncommon but a higher proportion of such pregnancies are ectopic: ectopic pregnancy must be excluded
guideline.citation: Faculty of Sexual and Reproductive Healthcare. FSRH Clinical Guideline: Intrauterine Contraception. London: FSRH; 2023.

rationale: Contraception lowers the chance of pregnancy but not the proportion of pregnancies that are ectopic; NICE NG126 requires a pregnancy test in every woman of reproductive age with abdominal pain. Left-sided pain should not steer the engine to diverticulitis at 29.
